title: StoryBrand Framework - SB7
subtitle: Your website, pitch deck, or marketing copy is confusing. People spend time on your
useWhen: website and leave without understanding what you do or why it matters to them. Your message is accurate it just doesn't land.
howToUse: Donald Miller's StoryBrand framework, published in 2017, is built on a single insight: customers don't care about your story, they care about their story, and whether you have a role in it. The SB7 structure positions the customer as the Hero, gives them a Guide (your brand), names the Problem (external, internal, and philosophical), provides a Plan, issues a Call to Action, describes Success, and shows what's at stake in Failure. When your marketing follows this structure, confused prospects become engaged ones.
steps: Never position your brand as the hero you are the guide who helps the hero succeed.
Name all three problem layers: external (practical), internal (emotional), philosophical (why it's wrong).
The plan must be simple three steps maximum. Complexity kills action.

Use this structure for your website homepage first, then apply it to email, ads, and pitches. Clarify your message so customers stop, listen, and act The most common StoryBrand mistake is failing to name the internal problem. The external problem is what they Google. The internal problem is what keeps them awake. Customers buy solutions to external problems but they buy from brands that understand their internal ones. Name the internal problem explicitly in your copy. PRO TIP
promptBody:
I PROMPT — COPY & PASTE READY
Act as a StoryBrand messaging consultant using Donald Miller's SB7.
My business          :  [WHAT YOU DO AND WHO YOU SERVE]
Customer's goal    :  [WHAT THE CUSTOMER WANTS TO ACHIEVE]
                                    Build the full SB7 for my brand:
CHARACTER         :   Who is the hero, describe them specifically
PROBLEM              :   External (practical), Internal (emotional), Philosophical (why it's 
                                     wrong that this exists)
GUIDE                     :   My brand's empathy and authority
PLAN                        :  3 simple steps to work with me
CALL TO ACTION  :  One direct CTA and one transitional CTA
SUCCESS                 :  What their life looks like after
FAILURE                  :  What's at stake if they don't act
Then write a one-sentence brand tagline using this structure.
